subject: Pathology
vignette: A 64-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history presents with cough and hemoptysis. Chest imaging shows a large hilar mass, and biopsy confirms small cell lung cancer. Serum sodium is 118 mEq/L, serum osmolality is low, urine osmolality is inappropriately high, and urine sodium is elevated. He is clinically euvolemic and has no diuretic use.
question: Which of the following best explains this patient's electrolyte abnormality?

options.text: Ectopic production of antidiuretic hormone
Ectopic production of parathyroid hormone-related peptide
Ectopic production of adrenocorticotropic hormone
Ectopic production of erythropoietin
Antibodies against presynaptic calcium channels at the neuromuscular junction

explanation_correct: This is the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, a paraneoplastic endocrine manifestation caused by ectopic ADH production and classically associated with small cell lung cancer. The result is euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine and elevated urine sodium. Small cell carcinoma of the lung is the classic tumor for both SIADH and ectopic ACTH.

explanation_incorrect.C: Ectopic ACTH from small cell lung cancer produces Cushing syndrome with hypercortisolism, not hypotonic hyponatremia with concentrated urine.
explanation_incorrect.D: Erythropoietin production causes paraneoplastic polycythemia, typically with renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, hemangioblastoma, or pheochromocytoma.
explanation_incorrect.E: Antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type calcium channels cause Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome with proximal muscle weakness, not hyponatremia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Parathyroid hormone-related peptide causes paraneoplastic hypercalcemia and is associated with squamous cell carcinomas of lung, head, and neck rather than small cell carcinoma.

educationalObjective: SIADH from ectopic ADH in small cell lung cancer causes euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 67-year-old man with a 45-pack-year smoking history presents with confusion, polyuria, constipation, and weakness. Laboratory studies show a serum calcium of 13.8 mg/dL with a low parathyroid hormone level and an elevated parathyroid hormone-related peptide level. Chest imaging reveals a centrally located lung mass, and biopsy shows keratinizing cells with intercellular bridges.
question: Which of the following best accounts for the hypercalcemia in this patient?

options.text: Ectopic ACTH secretion
Increased 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 production by the tumor
Ectopic antidiuretic hormone secretion
Parathyroid hormone-related peptide secretion by a squamous cell carcinoma
Direct osteolytic destruction by bone metastases

explanation_correct: Squamous cell carcinomas of the lung, head, and neck classically cause paraneoplastic hypercalcemia through secretion of parathyroid hormone-related peptide, which raises serum calcium while suppressing true PTH. Renal, bladder, breast, and ovarian carcinomas can also do this, and lymphoma causes hypercalcemia through increased 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3. The keratinizing histology with intercellular bridges identifies the squamous lineage.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ectopic ACTH causes Cushing syndrome with hypercortisolism and is classically associated with small cell lung cancer rather than squamous cell carcinoma.
explanation_incorrect.B: Increased calcitriol production is the mechanism of hypercalcemia in lymphoma, not the PTHrP mechanism described here.
explanation_incorrect.E: The vignette describes a humoral mechanism with suppressed PTH and elevated PTHrP; osteolytic bone metastases cause hypercalcemia through local bone destruction without elevated PTHrP.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ectopic ADH produces hyponatremia from SIADH, and it is classically associated with small cell lung cancer.

educationalObjective: PTHrP from squamous cell carcinoma of the lung causes paraneoplastic hypercalcemia; lymphoma causes it via calcitriol.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 59-year-old woman with a 5-cm pancreatic head mass presents with painless jaundice and weight loss. Over several weeks she has noted recurring, migrating, tender subcutaneous cords along the superficial veins of her legs and arms that appear in different locations each time. Ultrasound confirms superficial venous thrombosis without deep vein involvement. She has no known thrombophilia.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this patient's paraneoplastic finding?

options.text: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis with sterile platelet thrombi on heart valves
Sign of Leser-Trelat from a GI adenocarcinoma
Acanthosis nigricans from gastric adenocarcinoma
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy from lung adenocarcinoma
Trousseau syndrome, a migratory superficial thrombophlebitis associated with adenocarcinoma, especially pancreatic

explanation_correct: Trousseau syndrome is migratory superficial thrombophlebitis occurring as a paraneoplastic phenomenon, most commonly with adenocarcinomas, especially pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The recurrent, migrating nature of the thromboses in different venous segments is the classic descriptor. Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis is a related hypercoagulable paraneoplastic manifestation but involves sterile platelet thrombi on heart valves.

explanation_incorrect.A: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis is a paraneoplastic hypercoagulable state producing sterile valvular thrombi, but the finding here is recurrent superficial venous thrombosis in the limbs.
explanation_incorrect.C: Acanthosis nigricans produces hyperpigmented velvety plaques in the axillae and neck and is classically linked to gastric adenocarcinoma.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy causes digital clubbing, arthralgia, and periostosis of tubular bones and is associated with lung adenocarcinoma.
explanation_incorrect.B: The sign of Leser-Trelat is the sudden eruption of multiple seborrheic keratoses, not migratory venous thrombosis.

educationalObjective: Trousseau syndrome is migratory superficial thrombophlebitis, most often with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 61-year-old woman with a long smoking history develops progressive proximal muscle weakness, particularly of the hip girdle, along with dry mouth and constipation. On examination, deep tendon reflexes are diminished at rest but increase markedly after brief maximal voluntary contraction. There is no ptosis and no improvement with the ice pack test. Chest imaging reveals a central lung mass.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and causative tumor?

options.text: Myasthenia gravis associated with thymoma
Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration associated with ovarian cancer
Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome associated with small cell lung cancer
Paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis associated with anti-Hu antibodies
Opsoclonus-myoclonus ataxia syndrome associated with neuroblastoma

explanation_correct: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome is caused by antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type calcium channels at the neuromuscular junction, reducing acetylcholine release. It produces proximal muscle weakness with hyporeflexia that classically improves after brief maximal voluntary contraction, and autonomic symptoms such as dry mouth are common. It is most commonly paraneoplastic in adults and associated with small cell lung cancer.

explanation_incorrect.A: Myasthenia gravis involves antibodies against postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors, causes fatigable weakness with ptosis, and is associated with thymoma rather than small cell lung cancer.
explanation_incorrect.D: Paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis with anti-Hu antibodies causes psychiatric disturbance, memory deficits, seizures, and dyskinesias rather than isolated proximal weakness.
explanation_incorrect.E: Opsoclonus-myoclonus ataxia syndrome causes dancing eyes and dancing feet and occurs with neuroblastoma in children or small cell lung cancer in adults, but the reflex facilitation after contraction points to the neuromuscular junction.
explanation_incorrect.B: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration presents with ataxia from antibodies against Purkinje cell antigens and is associated with gynecologic and breast cancers, not with presynaptic calcium channel antibodies.

educationalObjective: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (presynaptic P/Q-type calcium channel antibodies) is associated with small cell lung cancer.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 48-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer treated 2 years ago now presents with flushing episodes, watery diarrhea, and new-onset tricuspid regurgitation with right-sided heart failure. A 24-hour urine test shows markedly elevated 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid. Imaging demonstrates a hepatic mass and no evidence of recurrence at the primary breast site.
question: Which of the following paraneoplastic or tumor-related findings best fits this presentation?

options.text: Cushing syndrome from ectopic ACTH secretion
Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration from anti-Yo antibodies
Pure red cell aplasia from a thymoma
Hypogammaglobulinemia from Good syndrome
Carcinoid syndrome from a neuroendocrine tumor metastatic to the liver

explanation_correct: Neuroendocrine tumors of the carcinoid type secrete serotonin and other vasoactive substances, and when metastatic to the liver the products bypass hepatic first-pass metabolism and produce carcinoid syndrome with flushing, secretory diarrhea, and right-sided valvular fibrosis such as tricuspid regurgitation. Elevated urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid, the serotonin metabolite, is confirmatory. Neuroendocrine tumors are also marked by chromogranin and neuron-specific enolase.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ectopic ACTH produces hypercortisolism with hypertension, weight gain, and hyperglycemia, and is classically associated with small cell lung cancer rather than flushing and diarrhea.
explanation_incorrect.C: Pure red cell aplasia is a paraneoplastic hematologic manifestation of thymoma producing anemia with low reticulocytes, not vasoactive symptoms with valvular disease.
explanation_incorrect.D: Good syndrome is hypogammaglobulinemia associated with thymoma and causes recurrent infections rather than flushing and diarrhea.
explanation_incorrect.B: Anti-Yo antibodies against Purkinje cell antigens cause cerebellar degeneration with ataxia and are associated with gynecologic and breast cancers, not with elevated 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid.

educationalObjective: Carcinoid syndrome from liver-metastatic neuroendocrine tumor causes flushing, diarrhea, right-sided valvular disease, and elevated urinary 5-HIAA.
